gaps.wanted: Whether the NCS 5011 is on sale. The one held document is silent; the intake grid marks every NCS model unknown. An end-of-sale notice or the product page would settle it.

A flat front and rear elevation, or a photograph taken square on. The guide's Figures 5 and 6 are greyscale three-quarter views, so every position is estimated and no printed numeral or legend can be read.

The legends printed beside the ports, lamps and jacks. None is resolved in the held figures, so none is drawn. The one legend drawn is the model name, NCS 5011, below the left end of the ports: an estimate of where the vendor prints it, since the figures do not show it.

The two 10GE SFP+ ports the guide lists under Ports (Chapter 1). Figures 6 and 12 show a small block at the left end of the port side that cannot be resolved into cages, so their position, and whether they are stacked, is not read and they are not placed.
The USB interface "on fan side of the router" (Features). Figure 5 resolves two stacked jacks and no USB port, so it is not placed.

The rack-mount kit as a kit contract: part numbers, the dimensions of the bracket, guide and slider rail, and the rack depth range. The guide gives a parts list whose counts disagree: Table 10 has four brackets, sixteen M4 x 7 mm screws, four guides and two slider rails; Appendix A's accessory kit NCS-5011-ACSR has two brackets, two guides, two sliders and sixteen M4 x 6 mm screws. It gives a rack requirement of 23.5 to 34.0 in between the outside faces of the front and rear rails, and no part numbers.

The management jack's rate. Searched the guide for "10/100", "1000", "Gigabit" and "speed" beside the management interface: it names the interface and gives no rate for the jack, so the DCIM export writes the exporter's default for a management jack.
The fan module's power draw, and the chassis' own draw. Appendix C gives supply ratings only.

The air filters, which the guide draws but does not size or number. The port-side-intake builds take a three-piece filter on the faceplate (Figure 22: pieces A, B and C); the port-side-exhaust builds take clip-on filters on the supply and the fan fronts (Figures 23 and 24). The figures do not say which chassis they show. No part number, size or position is held for either.
The label on the fan side that covers the grounding holes (Figure 16) and the lug bracket. Its size and position are not read from the three-quarter figure.
A drawing of the underside and the side walls. The guide shows one side wall in three-quarter view only, with six bracket holes; its positions cannot be read.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port group qsfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Chapter 2, Airflow Direction: front-to-back is "port side intake" and back-to-front is "port side exhaust", set by the type of fan modules and power supplies, and it is not possible to mix airflow directions. The builds are configurations. THE GUIDE GIVES NO COLOUR FOR EITHER DIRECTION in text or in its greyscale figures, so no handle colour is set per configuration.

arrangement.note: READ OFF FIGURES 6 AND 12, which show the same face: one long dark band of cages along the port side, with a small block at its left end. Thirty-two cages are drawn as two rows of sixteen, the arrangement of a one-unit box with that many QSFP28 cages; the figures do not let the cages be counted. The column step is the 24.4 mm and the row step the 16.8 mm the library uses for a two-row QSFP28 block on the NCS 5001, and the block is centred on the 43.7 mm face and sits clear of the left-end block. Both are estimates.

colour.note: The face is a light grey with dark printing in the guide's greyscale figures; #c9cccf is chosen by eye, not sampled.

configuration-names.note: THE GUIDE GIVES NO CHASSIS PART NUMBER AND NO CODE FOR ANY BUILD. Its only orderable codes for this router are the supplies and fan modules (Tables 6 and 7) and the accessory kit NCS-5011-ACSR, and it says "power supply options need to be configured with the base chassis". The four builds are therefore one `kind: base` build (AC, port-side intake) and three `kind: example` builds, with no `part-numbers`: each says which supplies and fan modules it seats, and none is an orderable SKU.

console-and-management.note: Two RJ-45 jacks stacked between the fourth fan module and the right supply, the console over the management jack, as the library draws them on other Cisco boxes. Figure 5 shows a column of two stacked jacks there; the guide's text names a console and a management interface and gives no more. Which is which is the library's convention, not a reading.

dimensions.note: Table 13 (printed page 42): "1.72 x 17.3 x 22.5 in. (4.4 cm x 43.9 cm x 57.15 cm)". The inch figures are carried, converted to 43.7 x 439.4 x 571.5 mm; the centimetre figures round to 44, 439 and 571.5, within 0.4 mm of the same numbers. The guide's Cabinet and Rack Installation appendix states a minimum of one rack unit. Whether the width includes the rack-mount brackets is not stated; the brackets are not drawn.

ears-and-kits.note: The `flush` position is the one Figure 12 draws: the front bracket bolts to the side of the chassis with its flange level with the port-side face. The guide says "any four of the holes in the front rack-mount bracket" meet "four of the six screw holes" in the chassis, so other positions exist, and none is measured; they are not written. NO KIT IS MODELLED: Table 10 lists the rack-mount kit as four brackets, sixteen M4 x 7 mm screws, four rack-mount guides and two slider rails, and Appendix A lists accessory kit NCS-5011-ACSR with two of each bracket, guide and slider and sixteen M4 x 6 mm screws, so the guide disagrees with itself on the counts and on the screw length; no document held gives a bracket's, a guide's or a slider's dimensions or the kit's depth range. See the gaps.

gate-1.note: FAILED AND SAID SO. Figures 5 and 6 are not orthographic: the near end of each face is drawn larger than the far end, so no px/mm can be derived from them and the aspect cannot be compared with Table 13's 439.4 by 43.7 mm. Only fractions of the face width were taken along the near edge, and the counts are the guide's. Every x and y on both faces is therefore estimated.

intake-mesh.note: Figures 5 and 6 show a black strip along the port-side edge of the lid, from near one side to near the other. It is on the lid, not on the face, so it is drawn in the top view and the front elevation stays plain. Its width, about 38 mm of the 571.5 mm lid, is read off the figures' foreshortened lid and is an estimate. THE GUIDE DOES NOT SAY WHAT THE STRIP IS. Its text says only that "a replaceable air filter is located on the front of the chassis" for port-side intake.

lamps.note: Appendix E, Table 23: a "Power LED" at the "Front of Chassis" (green solid on: system on and operating normally; green off: router powered off; amber on: fault condition), and on each supply an OK lamp (green) and a FAILED lamp (amber), Table 24. No port lamp, link lamp or fan lamp is described, so none is drawn; the chassis lamp's position on the port side is a guess at the block at the left end.

lifecycle.note: SALE STATUS IS UNKNOWN. The guide, in 66 pages, says nothing about end-of-sale or end-of-life, and no other document for this model is held; a revision date is not a status. No end-of-sale date is written.

port-order.note: THE GUIDE PRINTS NO PORT NUMBER IN ANY FIGURE AND NONE IS RESOLVED IN THE ARTWORK, so no numeral is drawn. The ids port-1 to port-32 follow the library's convention for stacked cages, down each column with the upper cage first. That order is a choice and not a reading. The guide's breakout text names interfaces (controller optics 0/0/0/0 is "port 0") and these are not recorded as port names.

ports.note: Chapter 1, Ports: "32 x 100G QSFP28-100 ports" and "2 x 10GE SFP + ports". The overview says "32 QSFP+/QSFP28 ports" without the SFP+, and that the system supports 10GE, 25GE, 40GE, 50GE and 100GE with 4x10G, 4x25G and 2x50G breakout for copper optics. Features: "A management, console, and the USB interface on fan side of the router". THE TWO SFP+ PORTS ARE NOT DRAWN: Figures 6 and 12 show a small block at the left end of the port side that cannot be resolved into cages at the figures' size, so they are a gap and not a guess. The USB port is a gap for the same reason on the fan side.

rear-face.note: Figure 5 (back, fan side), left to right as drawn: a supply, four fan modules, a block holding two stacked jacks, a supply. Module widths are fractions of the face width along its near edge: a supply reads about a fifth, each fan about an eighth, the jack block a thirtieth; the module sizes are the library's, with the fan width taken as the remainder of the face. Slot height is the one-rack-unit face less a little clearance. A label on the fan side covers the grounding holes ("remove the label on the rear side (fan side) of the router to expose the ground mounting holes", Figure 16); its position is not drawn.

sources.note: One document: Hardware Installation Guide for Cisco NCS 5000 Series Routers, first published 2015-12-23, last modified 2019-01-31 (https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/iosxr/ncs5000/hardware-install/b-ncs5000-hardware-installation-guide.pdf). It is an old revision and a newer one may exist. HELD AND SEARCHED FOR THIS MODEL: the guide's text and figures (5, 6, 12, 13, 16 and 22 to 24 were read), and the intake notes for the NCS line. NOT HELD: a data sheet, a NetBox device type or elevation, a photograph, a 3D model. THE GUIDE'S FACE FIGURES (5 and 6) ARE GREYSCALE THREE-QUARTER VIEWS at 759 x 464 and 760 x 474 px, and Figures 12 and 13 show the port side and the side wall in the same projection; there is no flat front or rear elevation, so every position below is read off a perspective drawing.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (the upper cage upright over the lower turned 180), by the rule and not by observation: the figures' resolution does not show which way the cages' lips face.

weight.note: THE GUIDE'S TWO UNITS DISAGREE. Table 13: "Cisco NCS 5011 with two 650W power supplies, and four fan modules, 22.2 lb (10.6 kg)"; 22.2 lb is 10.07 kg, not 10.6. The pound figure is carried in the note because Chapter 2 repeats it ("The Cisco NCS 5011 with two power supplies, weighs 22.2 lbs"), so two places print 22.2 lb and one prints 10.6 kg. It is a loaded weight, so no empty-chassis weight is written.
